### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order to avoid mistakes. | # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips | |---|------------|----------------|------| | 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Decide what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office work, etc.) and set a budget. | Use online PC builders (PCPartPicker, BuildMyPC) to compare prices and check compatibility. | | 2 | **Choose Components** | Pick CPU, motherboard, RAM, GPU, storage, PSU, case, cooling, and peripherals. | • **CPU + Motherboard**: Match socket (e.g., Intel LGA 1700, AMD AM5).
• **RAM**: DDR5/DDR4, 16 GB is a good baseline.
• **GPU**: Depends on workload; 3060/3070 for gaming, RTX 4090 for high‑end.
• **Storage**: NVMe SSD for OS + SSD/HDD combo for bulk.
• **PSU**: 80+ Gold, 650–850 W (or more for high‑end GPUs).
• **Case**: ATX mid‑tower or mini‑ITX if space is tight. | | 3 | **Gather Tools & Workspace** | You’ll need a Phillips‑head screwdriver, anti‑static wrist strap (optional), cable ties, and a clean, flat surface. | Work on a non‑conductive surface (wood, plastic). | | 4 | **Prepare the Case** | Remove side panels, lay the case flat, and ground yourself (touch metal). | Keep screws handy; they’re often reused. | | 5 | **Install the Power Supply** | Slide PSU into its tray, secure with screws, and route cables to the back. | Make sure the fan faces outward (or inward if the case has a rear exhaust). | | 6 | **Mount the Motherboard** | Align standoffs with motherboard holes, screw it in place. | Double‑check that all standoffs match the motherboard’s layout. | | 7 | **Install the CPU** | Open the CPU socket latch, align the CPU (gold triangle), gently place it, lock the latch. | Don’t force; the socket will guide it. | | 8 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install Cooler** | If your cooler doesn’t have pre‑applied paste, spread a pea‑size amount on the CPU. Mount the cooler, secure it, and connect the fan/VRM header. | For air coolers, use the mounting bracket; for liquid coolers, attach the pump to the motherboard. | | 9 | **Insert RAM** | Open the DIMM slots, align the notch, press until clicks. | Install in pairs for dual‑channel (e.g., slots 1 & 3). | | 10 | **Mount Storage** | For NVMe SSDs, slide into the M.2 slot and screw. For 2.5″ SSD/HDD, use the drive bay or mounting brackets. | Label SATA cables if you have multiple drives. | | 11 | **Install the GPU** | Remove the appropriate expansion slot covers from the case, insert the GPU into the top PCI‑e x16 slot, screw it in. | Connect 8‑pin/6‑pin power connectors from PSU to GPU. | | 12 | **Connect Motherboard Power** | Attach the 24‑pin ATX and 8‑pin EPS cables from PSU to motherboard. | Ensure cables are snug but not over‑tightened. | | 13 | **Connect Front Panel & USB** | Refer to the motherboard manual for exact pinouts. | Connect power button, reset button, HDD LED, front USB, audio jacks. | | 14 | **Cable Management** | Route cables neatly, use cable ties, and keep airflow unobstructed. | Avoid blocking fans or vents. | | 15 | **Double‑Check Connections** | Verify all cables, screws, and components are secure. | Look for any loose screws that could touch components. | | 16 | **Close the Case** | Replace side panels, secure screws. | Keep the case open for a few minutes to let any static dissipate. | | 17 | **First Boot** | Connect monitor, keyboard, mouse, and power cable. Turn on PSU, then press the power button. | Watch for POST (Power‑On Self Test) beep codes or screen output. | | 18 | **Enter BIOS/UEFI** | Press the key shown on screen (Del, F2, Esc). | Set boot priority to your OS drive, enable XMP for RAM. | | 19 | **Install Operating System** | Use a USB flash drive with Windows 10/11, Ubuntu, etc. | Follow on‑screen prompts, install drivers after OS is up. | | 20 | **Install Drivers & Updates** | Download latest GPU drivers, chipset drivers, and Windows updates. | Use manufacturer sites (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel). | | 21 | **Test & Benchmark** | Run stress tests (Prime95, 3DMark, Cinebench) to ensure stability. | Monitor temperatures (HWMonitor, MSI Afterburner). | | 22 | **Enjoy & Maintain** | Keep drivers updated, clean dust every 3–6 months, monitor temperatures. | Consider adding a second PSU cable for future upgrades. | --- #### Quick Checklist - [ ] CPU + Cooler - [ ] Motherboard + Standoffs - [ ] RAM - [ ] GPU - [ ] Storage (NVMe/SSD/HDD) - [ ] PSU - [ ] Case - [ ] Front panel connectors - [ ] Cables (SATA, power, USB, audio) - [ ] BIOS settings (XMP, boot order) - [ ] OS installation media - [ ] Drivers & updates --- #### Common Pitfalls & Fixes | Issue | Likely Cause | Fix | |-------|--------------|-----| | PC won’t power on | PSU not connected or switched off | Check PSU switch, cables, and ensure PSU is plugged in. | | No display | GPU not seated or power connector missing | Re‑seat GPU, connect power cables. | | Overheating | Poor airflow or inadequate cooling | Re‑arrange cables, add case fans, upgrade cooler. | | BIOS not detecting SSD | SATA cable mis‑connected or SSD not powered | Verify SATA power and data cables, try another port. | | Random restarts | PSU insufficient wattage | Upgrade PSU or reduce power draw. | --- #### Resources - **PCPartPicker** – Build planner & price comparison. - **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware. - **Manuals** – Keep motherboard, PSU, and case manuals handy (PDFs online). - **Forums** – r/buildapc on Reddit for troubleshooting. --- ### Final Thought Building a PC is a rewarding project that gives you control over performance, aesthetics, and future upgrades. Take your time, double‑check every connection, and enjoy the process! If you hit a snag, feel free to ask for help—happy building!
